thread:
emily: Heads-up — customer FinMetrics reports truncated streaming responses. The client gets a partial JSON object (trailing comma / missing final brace) and there is no finish_reason or final SSE 'data: [DONE]'. They say it usually happens when their SDK refreshes the auth token mid-request. Repro steps they gave below.

javier: Thanks — can you paste the exact curl repro and any server-side logs?

emily: Curl repro they used: 
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" 
     -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" 
     -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" 
     -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streaming/generate 
     -d '{"model":"rw-large", "input":"<long prompt>\", "max_tokens":2000, "stream":true}'
```
Behavior: client receives a stream of `data: { ... }\n` events, then suddenly the stream ends with a trailing comma (",\n") and EOF. No final `data: [DONE]` event and the captured last JSON fragment cannot be parsed. Client attempts a reconnect (they attach last_event_id) and the resume response includes the same partial fragment (leftover comma) so their parser fails.

leo: Any proxy in front? Fastly/nginx that might drop the tail?

emily: We have a runtime log from our serving node around the incident: 
```
2024-11-01T15:04:12.345Z service=runtime request_id=fin-req-abc123 status=200 bytes_sent=2834 connection_closed_early=true proxy_err=499 note=\"client closed connection during send\"
2024-11-01T15:04:12.346Z service=runtime request_id=fin-req-abc123 shard=shard-7 stream_writer=EPIPE
2024-11-01T15:04:12.347Z model=rw-large seq=198 kv_cache=flushed reason=partial_write
```
Also an nginx access log sample: `... 499 \"POST /v1/streaming/generate HTTP/1.1\"` which indicates the client closed connection.

ops_oncall: That aligns with mid-request client-side token swap closing the socket. If client aborts during token refresh their local HTTP lib may close underlying connection and then try to open a new one to resume — but resume machinery might replay a tail fragment or leave a dangling comma. Two hypotheses: (1) client closes/aborts and our runtime writes tail concurrently leading to partial flush, or (2) an intermediate proxy buffers and cuts the last chunk when the upstream connection drops.

javier: Can we reproduce with an aggressive client token refresh? emily, can you give a minimal Node repro to simulate their SDK?

emily: Minimal Node repro (they used node-fetch + in-house auth refresher): 
```js
// start streaming request
const res = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, Accept: 'text/event-stream' }, body: JSON.stringify(payload) });
// read some events, then simulate token rotate on same SDK instance
// old code: fetch controller.abort() then re-issue a new request with new token and try to resume
// this sequence sometimes leaves server-side writer mid-flush and client sees truncated JSON
```
Workaround the customer used: keep long-lived preflight token for stream lifecycle or open a dedicated short-lived session token that is renewed before streaming begins.

ops_oncall: For immediate mitigation: ask them to avoid rotating the token while a stream is active. If they must, advise them to gracefully close/await the stream end before token swap. We should also add server-side hardening: ensure runtime completes final flusher even if client closed? But that risks writing to closed fd. We can at least ensure we emit final `data: [DONE]` and flush before closing the socket when possible.

leo: From infra side, can we check edge/proxy timeouts and buffering? If the client closes the connection, nginx returns 499 and the upstream may still be trying to write; that can leave a partial TLS record. Let's also check Fastly or CDN logs for any mid-chunk resets.

emily: I collected a HAR from the customer's browser session and a tcpdump around the incident. HAR shows: final event chunk arrives in partial 1270 bytes, then the client TCP FIN immediately after. tcpdump shows last packet payload ends with `...,"last_field": "value",}` actually missing trailing brace in reassembled stream.

javier: Thanks — next steps for eng-runtime: (1) reproduce with a scripted token rotate that aborts and reopens mid-stream, (2) add additional instrumentation to detect whether we successfully wrote the final SSE sentinel, (3) consider adding a short server-side retry to emit final sentinel to logs for post-mortem (can't always write to client).

support-bot: Ticket created: SUP-4821 (priority P2) assigned to eng-oncall. Please attach repro artifacts.

sophie: I've attached the customer's HAR, tcpdump, and the full runtime request_id traces to SUP-4821. Also noted that the customer briefly hit a quota limit earlier the same day which triggered a token refresh in their infra — likely correlated.

ops_oncall: If we can't change runtime semantics quickly, add an entry to support KB: \"Streaming & auth rotation — avoid rotating tokens while stream active; if unavoidable, use a new connection and accept that the server may not emit a resume-friendly final sentinel.\" Include recommended client-side parsing: be tolerant of a trailing comma or attempt JSON reassembly using last valid object boundary, and request the server logs / request_id to escalate.

javier: For the immediate customer response: 1) ask them to retry with token TTL extended during long streams, 2) provide Node + curl repro we used, 3) ask them to capture tcpdump and HAR and send request_id if it occurs again.

emily: I'll send the customer the repro and mitigation. Logging: we'll add an alert rule to flag `stream_writer=EPIPE` + `connection_closed_early=true` spikes.

sophie: Closing loop — will update SUP-4821 with mitigation steps and ask eng to prioritize a safe guard to emit a final sentinel to logs so support can show the customer whether the server finished encoding the final object even if client dropped.

leo: I'll follow up on proxy buffering settings and report back in the ticket.

emily: Thanks all :thumbsup: If we find a clear runtime fix path I'll file an RFC for the change.
